content: The American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) is the largest organization in the United States dedicated to nursing credentialing. It operates as a subsidiary of the American Nurses Association (ANA). The ANCC provides credentialing programs in five nursing specialties: gerontology, medical-surgical, pediatrics, perinatal, and psychiatric and mental health nursing. In 1966, the ANA amended its bylaws to include the recognition of professional achievement in nursing practice and the establishment of certification boards for each division to define specialized criteria for certification. By 1973, the ANA had initiated a national certification program to acknowledge excellence in clinical nursing practice. By 1974, five practice divisions had developed certification guidelines, and the first certification examinations were administered that same year. The ANCC was formally established as a separately incorporated nonprofit organization in June 1990, following recommendations from the ANA’s Commission on Assessment and Renewal. In 1991, the ANCC became a subsidiary of the ANA, and the ANA’s certification, accreditation, and Magnet Recognition Programs were transferred to the ANCC. Currently, the ANCC administers a variety of programs to achieve its goals. The Accreditation Program, established in 1974, recognizes organizations and programs that provide high-quality continuing education for nurses. It also offers a voluntary peer review process to establish standards for continuing education and assess adherence to those standards. The Magnet Recognition Program®, which began as a task force in 1983, acknowledges hospitals that attract and retain highly qualified nurses committed to delivering quality patient care. This program developed the Magnet Model, which organizes 14 Forces of Magnetism into five components: transformational leadership, structural empowerment, exemplary professional practice, new knowledge and innovations, and empirical outcomes. The Pathway to Excellence® Program was acquired by the ANCC in 2007. Originally started by the Texas Nurses Association under a different name, it aimed to improve nurse retention and care quality in small, rural hospitals. The program recognizes hospitals that create environments where nurses can thrive and has established 12 standards that healthcare institutions must meet to earn recognition. The Institute for Credentialing Innovation®, created in 1998, develops and manages innovative educational products and services to support the ANCC’s accreditation, certification, Magnet, and Pathway programs. These offerings include online learning, review manuals, seminars, regional workshops, symposiums, national conferences, and consulting services. The ANCC’s Institute for Credentialing Research was formally established in 2005 to support research activities related to its programs and to promote studies demonstrating the importance of credentialing in achieving excellence in nursing and healthcare. In 1999, the ANCC established Credentialing International in response to requests for assistance from other countries. However, this initiative was dissolved in 2009, and international outreach responsibilities were integrated into each of the ANCC’s program areas.
